synopsis: Evidence reuse across machine models is described as the biggest validation lever but the least documented; extension requires similarity arguments and bridging evidence, not automatic inheritance [f366, f189, f7569]. The proposed method uses a parameterized family model validated at envelope corners, a documented change assessment, and targeted bridge tests; a variant inside the validated family hull receives reduced physical tests, typically brake calibration and sensor field-of-view and detection checks [f7573, f12368]. Sensor relocation can invalidate the envelope even with unchanged software: blind-area geometry changes, height shifts degrade neural reconstruction more than sideways shifts, and learned sensor models extrapolate weakly to new viewpoints [f12370, f11552, f82, f4489]. Explicit geometry and physics-based sensor models offer useful transfer capabilities, but viewpoint-valid geometry alone does not validate appearance or sensor response [f4181, f4466, f4174]. Rail, aerospace and nuclear practice provide formal extension precedents, yet no published off-road variant-transfer example or formally accepting off-road regulator was found; neither the removable physical-test count for dozens of variants nor an accepted transferred-brake-model test count was established [f7570, f7571, f7572, f7574, f2943, f1960, f6557].
